assessment.reason: The model projects roughly 0.56 assists against a 0.5 line. Its estimate stays at or above the +165 break-even even at the low end of the sensitivity band. The cushion is thin and no material blocker is identified.
assessment.model_case: 164 appearances support the expected-role projection at 17.1 minutes, with the latest game on Oct 17. The main weakness is that line and power-play assignment are unverified, and assist output depends heavily on power-play usage.
assessment.price_case: Main line at +165 requires about 3-in-8. Fair odds are near +135 and the minimum is about +160, so modest price drift removes the case. One comparison book is not consensus.
assessment.context_case: Two Pittsburgh forwards and defensemen appear on the injury table. Linemate effects are unclear, and Malkin's absence from the table does not confirm he is healthy.

qualitative_review.countercase: The low-band estimate sits barely above break-even, and a 10x weight blend toward market cuts the edge to small. Losing power-play time or facing a strong Vejmelka start could push the true rate below the +165 hurdle.

assessment.reason: The model's projected mean of 0.26 assists implies a short under price. The gap with the market is large. Several Toronto centers are listed out, and if Roslovic's usage expands, the model's historical ice-time basis may understate his opportunity.
assessment.model_case: The 15.7-minute projection rests on 164 appearances. Ice time and the power-play role may be stale if Toronto lineup absences elevate him; a usage increase is the mechanism that would erode the under.
assessment.price_case: At -200, the break-even is two-in-three. The model's fair price is near -336 against one comparison book. A large gap like this from a single book warrants scrutiny rather than confidence.
assessment.context_case: The Toronto table lists multiple centers on IR. San Jose coverage is missing, so opponent absences are unverified. Settlement rules are assumed rather than checked.
blocking_checks: Roslovic's line and power-play assignment given listed Toronto center absences: a top-six or PP1 role would raise his assist rate and could erase the under's margin

qualitative_review.countercase: If the center injuries push Roslovic up the lineup, the history-based projection likely understates his usage. The market's roughly two-in-three view would then be closer to fair, and -200 offers little.

findings.note: ESPN's game log has Malkin at 5 goals and 2 assists in 9 games this season. He has no assists or power-play assists in his last five games, and he played only 12:51 in the 6-2 loss at Vegas on Oct 17.
NHL.com's projected lineup for Oct 17 puts Malkin on the second line with Egor Chinakhov and Tommy Novak, behind Rakell-Crosby-Rust, at center on the right. He is not listed as injured.

Pittsburgh re-signed the now-40-year-old Malkin to a one-year, $5.5M deal for 2026-27. He had averaged a point per game or better in 16 of his 20 seasons, but this year's early output has leaned heavily toward goals.

NHL.com's projected lines for Oct. 17 had Roslovic on Toronto's top line with Auston Matthews and William Nylander, which gives him more chances at assists. This is from the previous game, not a confirmed lineup for tonight against the Sharks.

ESPN shows 3 goals and 3 assists in 9 games this season, averaging 16:47 of ice time, with only one power-play assist. His game log has 1 assist in his last 5 games and none in the Oct. 17 loss to the Islanders, though ESPN's summary still describes him as at home on the top line.
NHL.com's preview named Roslovic a fantasy sleeper who could set career highs and listed him on Matthews' line. He had 15 assists in 69 games for Edmonton last season.
